## Example 2.7 · i {#fv2-example-2-7-i .fv-lesson .proof-lesson .proof-compact}

```{=html}
<p>On the triangular pyramid <span data-math="ABCD"></span>, <span data-math="L"></span> is the midpoint of <span data-math="AB"></span>, <span data-math="M"></span> is the midpoint of <span data-math="AC"></span>, <span data-math="N"></span> is the midpoint of <span data-math="AD"></span>, <span data-math="P"></span> is the midpoint of <span data-math="CD"></span>, <span data-math="Q"></span> is the midpoint of <span data-math="BD"></span> and <span data-math="R"></span> is the midpoint of <span data-math="BC"></span>.</p><div class="proof-split"><div><div class="proof-diagram " data-proof-diagram="pyramid" role="img" aria-label="Triangular pyramid ABCD with all six edge midpoints labelled L, M, N, P, Q and R."></div></div><div><p>Let <span data-math="\underset{\sim}{b}=\overrightarrow{AB},\ \underset{\sim}{c}=\overrightarrow{AC}"></span> and <span data-math="\underset{\sim}{d}=\overrightarrow{AD}"></span>.</p><p>(i) Show that <span data-math="\overrightarrow{LP}=\frac12(-\underset{\sim}{b}+\underset{\sim}{c}+\underset{\sim}{d})."></span></p><p><span class="marks">(1 mark)</span></p></div></div>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet Example 2.7 · p. 23–24</div>

::: {.notes}
Source: 2023 HSC Mathematics Extension 2, Q15(b), 4 marks total. Choose A as the common origin. AL=b/2 and AP=(c+d)/2, so LP=AP−AL=(−b+c+d)/2. Alternative path L→A→C→P gives −b/2+c+(d−c)/2. The three edges from A are non-coplanar for a non-degenerate pyramid. Use the static diagram to trace a path; no 3D rotation controls.
:::
